meta.title: Journal of the Republic — Politicas
meta.description: A chronological daily record of the state: signed contracts, prints referred to committees, promulgations in the Collection of Laws, register roles and human-gate decisions — dated, cited, permanently linkable.

denik.kicker: the daily record of the republic
denik.title: Journal of the Republic
denik.lead: One day, one entry: contracts signed by companies tied to MPs, parliamentary prints referred to committees, promulgations in the Collection of Laws, register-role entries and removals, and human-gate decisions. Every row has a date and a source, and every day has a permanent address.

rule.body: The journal runs two streams, and every row states which clock dates it. effective rows carry the day the event happened according to its register (a contract signature, a role entry, a print step) — not the day ingest found it. recorded rows carry the day the fact entered the record: human-gate decisions (review_audit is an append-only log) and, since the bitemporal graph arrived, changes of the graph itself (change_event — a new tie, a tie change, a contract in the graph). What the graph recorded before the bitemporal-migration epoch, the “recorded” stream honestly does not carry — nothing is stamped retroactively. Contracts are listed only for companies with an owner/operator-class tie — contracts of institutions where an MP merely sits on a body are that institution's money.

meta.title: Evidence Journal — Politicas
meta.description: The human gate's public gazette: every verification, rejection or request for more evidence on an MP ↔ company tie as a dated, citable record with links to the primary registers.

dukazy.title: Evidence Journal
dukazy.lead: Every decision that passes human review — verifying or rejecting an MP ↔ company tie, requesting additional evidence, a signed forensic report — becomes a public, dated, permanently linkable record here. The gate itself is a publication event.

method.body: What is published: the ruling, the subject, the date, the reviewer's role and links to the primary registers — never the reviewer's working notes. “Additional evidence requested” is not a verdict: the tie keeps waiting for review. The record's verifiability (audit trail and vault heads) is held by the <admin>operations console /admin</admin>.

meta.title: Civic Inbox — Politicas
meta.description: Follow MPs, parliamentary bills, companies and municipalities — no account, follows live only in your browser. On every visit the inbox shows what changed in the record since the last one: dated, cited entries from the republic journal and the evidence journal.

hero.kicker: a personal inbox of the record
hero.title: Civic Inbox
hero.lead: Follow MPs, bills, companies or municipalities — and on every visit the inbox shows you what changed in the record since the previous one. Every row is a dated journal entry with its source; the inbox adds nothing, it only filters.

rule.body1: Following works without an account: the list lives in your browser (localStorage). When news is requested, though, that whole list travels in the request ADDRESS (?e=poslanec:…) — that is by design, because the address is also your subscription: it can be saved or passed on, and whoever has it sees the same selection. No cookies, no sign-in, nothing stored on the server; the keys are struck from server telemetry and only their count remains. What the server sees, as with any other page, is the request IP address — the inbox does not remove that and does not claim otherwise. Journal entries are dated by day, so the “since your last visit” threshold is daily: the day of the last visit is counted whole again — better to show an entry twice than to withhold one.
rule.firstVisit: A first visit has no stamp — the last {days} days of the record are shown.
rule.body2: The badge in the sidebar follows a stricter rule: after a visit the inbox notes how many of that day's entries you had in front of you, and the badge then leaves them out — which is why it goes dark after a visit even though the visit day still counts whole above the threshold. Only the count from that same day is subtracted; nothing else. The page stays lenient — the two rules differ on purpose.
rule.body3: What the inbox CANNOT see: for the contribution index recompute it reports only THAT it ran — the graph holds only current values and no previous ones, so how far a score moved cannot be derived from it and the inbox does not claim it. The row therefore carries the pass number, the formula ref and a link to the <metodika>methodology</metodika>. It is reported only when the whole chamber holds one pass; half a recompute is not a fact. The kind summary in an entity header counts the whole delta, even when only the first {cap} rows fit below it.

meta.title: Open Data Quality Atlas — Politicas
meta.description: Public quality grades for the sources politicas ingests: provenance coverage, freshness against cadence, Merkle seal integrity, completeness measured by admitted gaps. Every score ships with its rule printed next to it; a dimension without evidence is “unrated”, never zero.

hero.kicker: the public quality atlas of the data layer’s sources
hero.title: Open Data Quality Atlas
hero.lead: Every source politicas ingests gets a public grade here: provenance coverage, freshness against its declared cadence, the integrity of Merkle seals, and completeness measured by upstream’s admitted gaps. Every score carries its rule printed verbatim next to the number — and a dimension without evidence is honestly “unrated”, never zero. The traps you will run into here (sentinel birth dates, merged K votes, placeholder years 2925) are the same institutional memory that politicas’ analytical runs read.

methodology.body: Scores 0–100 are computed deterministically from the current state of the store (entity tables with the provenance quartet, the ingest_run table, source contexts). Cadence vocabulary: age of the last refresh ≤ cadence is “fresh”, up to {stale}× cadence “aging”, beyond {stale}× cadence “stale”; the freshness score falls to zero at {zero}× cadence. Cadence is politicas’ declared expectation, not the publisher’s SLA. Low completeness is a statement about the publisher’s data, not about the processing — gaps are admitted, not hidden. A dimension without evidence is “unrated” with a reason and does not enter the composite.

storeDown.body: The atlas cannot be built right now — the store is unavailable in this environment. This page cannot say how the sources are doing; the scores are not zero, they are unreadable.
storeDown.source: source: store unavailable — no score is concealed or invented

sources.title: Sources
sources.aside: source: entity tables + ingest_run + source contexts (context-model)
sources.lead: {count} sources on record. A union of three views: sources with a processed context, sources with rows in the store, and sources with ingest runs — a source known from only one side is shown too, with an honest “unrated” wherever evidence is missing.

cards.sortRule: sorting rule: descending by the chosen score; “unrated” always sorts after rated — unrated is not zero even when sorting; ties are decided by the source key

coverage.label: provenance coverage
coverage.rule: 100 × (source rows linked to an ingest run / all source rows in the store), rounded. A row without ingest_run_id carries only partial provenance (source + url + fetched_at); a row with it is traceable back to the run that wrote it. A source with no rows = unrated.

freshness.label: freshness
freshness.rule: Age = today minus the finish of the source’s last successful ingest run. Score 100 at age ≤ cadence, then linear to 0 at age = 3× cadence. In words: ≤ cadence is “fresh”, ≤ 2× cadence “aging”, beyond 2× cadence “stale”. Cadence is politicas’ declared expectation, not the publisher’s SLA. Without a declared cadence or a successful run = unrated.

integrity.label: integrity
integrity.rule: 100 × (the source’s finished successful runs sealed with a Merkle root / all of the source’s finished successful runs), rounded. The seal is applied by LedgerRepository.sealIngestRun over every row the run wrote. A source with no finished successful run = unrated.

completeness.label: completeness
completeness.rule: 100 minus 10 points for every admitted upstream gap (KNOWN ISSUES in the source context, lib/analysis/context-model.ts), floored at 0. A low score is a statement about the publisher’s data, not about politicas’ processing — gaps are admitted, not hidden. A source without a processed context = unrated (undocumented ≠ complete).

card.source: source: entity tables (provenance quartet) + ingest_run (runs, Merkle roots from LedgerRepository.sealIngestRun) + source context (lib/analysis/context-model.ts)

meta.title: Data Releases — Politicas
meta.description: The graph of the republic released like software: YYYY.MM.DD versions, cardinality floors as the release gate, Merkle roots and a review hash-chain as proof of integrity, a downloadable snapshot with its size admitted.

hero.kicker: the public release train of the data layer
hero.title: Data Releases
hero.lead: The graph of the republic is released like software: every successful data ingest cuts a <mono>YYYY.MM.DD</mono> version, cardinality floors are the release gate, and the integrity of every release is provable by Merkle roots and the review hash-chain. What you download today you can cite — and anyone can verify it.

methodology.body: Version = the day of the last finished successful ingest run (the ingest_run table). A version that misses the cardinality floors (CARDINALITY_FLOORS) is marked “degraded” and is never “latest”. Floor verdicts are computed from the current state of the store — about historical versions this page claims nothing it could not prove. The snapshot is a cut of the derived graph (kg_node / kg_edge) capped at {nodeCap} nodes and {edgeCap} edges; any truncation is admitted in the limits field.
